title: United wins red-flagged Spa as G-Drive clinch the title
dek: Filipe Albuquerque and Phil Hanson won the rain-shortened 4 Hours of Spa for United from second on the grid, while pole-sitting G-Drive took the LMP2 title despite a penalty.

chapters.title: A title that needs only a podium
text: The 4 Hours of Spa-Francorchamps on 23 September 2018 was the penultimate round of the European Le Mans Series, and in LMP2 it was a title decider waiting to happen. G-Drive Racing's TDS-run Oreca #26 had won the previous three races and arrived 34 points clear of Racing Engineering's #24 Oreca, whose retirement at Silverstone had put a real dent in its hopes. Roman Rusinov and Andrea Pizzitola, who had started every round, led the drivers' standings by the same margin, with Jean-Eric Vergne sharing the car after missing the opener. A win or a second place at Spa would close out the teams' title and earn an automatic invitation to the 2019 Le Mans 24 Hours.

Forty cars were entered, 16 of them in LMP2. IDEC Sport's Ligier was back after missing Silverstone, but the team's plans were upended on Saturday when Lafargue's back trouble returned and he went to hospital. Gabriel Aubry was called up to join Paul Loup Chatin and Memo Rojas in the #28 Oreca, while Nicolas Minassian moved across to the #27 Ligier alongside Aurelien Panis and Erik Maris. Algarve Pro Racing's #25 had Matthew Mcmurry back in the seat vacated by Ate Dirk de Jong. United Autosports ran its two LMP2 Ligiers on Michelin tyres for the first time, and the paddock was busy with 2019 plans, with RLR MSport, Inter Europol Competition and Cool Racing all announcing LMP3-to-LMP2 step-ups that week.

Saturday morning's second practice was dominated by the weather. Vergne topped LMP2 on 2:02.348, but rain returned shortly after the start, bringing a Full Course Yellow and two red flags. Graff's two Orecas were hit hardest: James Allen crashed the #40 G-Drive-liveried car at Turn 13, and the #39 was also damaged, tearing a suspension mounting out of the tub. Graff had no spare, so TDS lent one and the team spent the rest of the day rebuilding around it. Between them the two cars managed only 11 laps in the session.

chapters.title: Vergne takes pole on the last lap
text: Vergne put the #26 on pole with a 2:00.735 at the very end of the session, his first pole in the European Le Mans Series and G-Drive's first of the season. Filipe Albuquerque had briefly taken provisional pole in the United Autosports #22 Ligier and ended up 0.177 seconds behind on 2:00.912, a strong first showing on Michelin tyres. The point for pole stretched G-Drive's championship lead to 35 before a lap had been raced.

Nelson Panciatici put the Duqueine Engineering Oreca #29 third on 2:01.251, with Chatin fourth for IDEC Sport and Gustavo Menezes fifth for APR-Rebellion, about nine tenths off the pole time. Norman Nato was sixth for Racing Engineering. Ben Hanley's DragonSpeed Oreca lined up seventh, and Will Stevens in the Panis Barthez Ligier tenth. Late in the session Mcmurry had a big moment over the kerbs at Eau Rouge, and the engine cover of the #25 Algarve Pro Ligier blew off onto the circuit, bringing out yellow flags.

With heavy rain forecast for Sunday, the stewards and team managers met on Saturday evening and brought the start forward from 12:30 to 10:45, with the finish rescheduled for 14:45, in the hope of running the bulk of the race before the worst of the weather arrived.

chapters.title: Pizzitola leads, then runs into trouble
text: Pizzitola led from pole while Chatin's #28 dived into the pits early for tyres. Nicolas Jamin then harried the G-Drive's rear wing in the Duqueine #29 for several laps before sweeping past at Fagnes. A 20-minute Safety Car for two LMP3 cars in trouble, one of them stopped on the Kemmel Straight, changed the order of the pit stops. Several teams took the chance to pit, including United, where Phil Hanson handed the #22 to Albuquerque. The split strategy cost track position, and the car had dropped to eighth, but it put Albuquerque in the car early on a wet and worsening track.

chapters.title: Albuquerque takes over as G-Drive unravels
text: After the restart Pizzitola was pressed by Menezes's APR-Rebellion #31, then ran through the gravel at Turn 14 and did so again on the next lap while avoiding a stopped LMP3 Ligier, dropping the points leader to ninth. He handed over to Vergne. Albuquerque meanwhile worked his way to the front around the turn of the first and second hours and built a lead of roughly five seconds over Julien Canal's #23 Panis Barthez Ligier, with Nato's Racing Engineering Oreca only 1.4 seconds further back.

Vergne's own stint went wrong when he tried to pass Ryan Cullen's #31 on the run to the final corner. He clipped Christian Ried's Proton Porsche #77, which spun across the wet grass into the side of the APR-Rebellion, and the stewards handed the G-Drive a two-minute stop-and-hold penalty.

chapters.title: Red flag, and a win declared
text: The #31 stopped on the Kemmel Straight with its damage, and with an LMP3 Ligier off at Turn 4 the Safety Car came out for the third time. As the rain grew heavier the race was red-flagged just after the two-hour mark and the cars were lined up on the pit straight. Race control later called the race off for good. Because the two-hour mark had been passed, the result stood and half points were awarded.

Albuquerque and Hanson were declared winners in the #22, with DragonSpeed's Oreca #21 of Hanley, Henrik Hedman and Nicolas Lapierre classified second, 1.862 seconds back and on the podium for the second race running. The #23 of Stevens, Timothe Buret and Canal completed the podium 8.702 seconds behind the winner. IDEC Sport's #28 finished fourth, Duqueine's #29 fifth and United's other Ligier #32 sixth. Racing Engineering's #24 was only seventh, and the penalised G-Drive crew ended up 12th in class.

chapters.title: G-Drive take the title the hard way
text: For United Autosports it was a first LMP2 win of the 2018 season, and the first for Albuquerque and Hanson as a pair in the European Le Mans Series. The car's pace in the wet and in qualifying suggested that the change to Michelin tyres had paid off. Albuquerque described a chaotic and often dangerous race, said Eau Rouge was especially difficult in the wet, and called the decision to stop the race the correct one. He had been hoping to build a big lead before handing back to Hanson, a plan the red flag cut short. United co-owner Zak Brown had called the team's season in the series disappointing before the start, and said the Ligier needed more pace and that a second round of performance adjustments should be pursued.

G-Drive's day was far scrappier, but it did not matter. Rusinov and Pizzitola were crowned LMP2 champions, with Vergne, and the team secured the title with a round to spare. With half points on offer and Racing Engineering only seventh, the Spanish team could not close the gap. The result earned G-Drive Racing an automatic place in the 2019 Le Mans 24 Hours.

Vergne's two-minute stop-and-hold for the collision with the Proton Porsche had dropped the car out of the top 10 at the time, but with Racing Engineering unable to profit, the title was never in real danger.

The ELMS now heads to Portimão for the season finale on 28 October, with the LMP2 titles already settled while the LMP3 and GTE championships stay open. The 2019 calendar, announced during the week, will drop the Red Bull Ring in favour of Barcelona.

facts.v: Jean-Eric Vergne took pole in the #26 G-Drive Oreca with a 2:00.735, 0.177 seconds ahead of Filipe Albuquerque's United Ligier.
